key_insight: Additively manufactured porous wall lattices can raise hydrogen flashback limits, with the coarsest structure giving the strongest protection.
engineering_relevance: Porous nozzle walls offer a practical design route to improve safety and operability in hydrogen combustors without significantly changing the core flow pattern.
method: Compared five jet-flame combustor nozzle configurations with different body-centered cubic lattice wall designs.
Varied lattice volume fraction and strut diameter in metal parts made by laser powder bed fusion.
Used flow-field measurements, flame imaging, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to track flame dynamics and flashback onset.
evidence_signal: Across equivalence ratios and Reynolds numbers of 9,000-12,000, the coarsest porous wall showed the clearest flashback-resistance improvement, while flow and flame shape changes remained minor.
watch_item: The benefit appears tied to cooling by unburnt mixture through the porous wall, so manufacturability, pressure loss, and durability must be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Effect of Additively Manufactured Wall Lattice Structures on Flashback Limits in a Hydrogen Jet Flame Combustor
